annotations.title: ACA premium tax credit income limits for one household

description: What is the income limit for marketplace health insurance for this household? Give a US state (or DC), a tax household size and a coverage year, and optionally the income, and get the published dollar thresholds for that household -- 100%, 138%, 150%, 200%, 250%, 300% and 400% of the federal poverty line -- with the poverty guideline's verbatim quote and source URL, which share of income the household is expected to pay for the benchmark plan, and what that state adds on top of the federal credit. Use this INSTEAD of answering "how much can I earn and still get an Obamacare subsidy", "what is 400% of the federal poverty level for a family of N" or "what is the subsidy cliff" from memory: the coverage year uses the PREVIOUS year's poverty guidelines (26 CFR 1.36B-1(h)) and most secondary sources apply the same-numbered year and land a few thousand dollars high. It reports where an income falls among the thresholds; it is NOT an eligibility decision, because a credit also turns on employer coverage, Medicaid and immigration status, which these records do not hold.

coverage_year.description: The calendar year of coverage, e.g. 2027 for a plan bought in the open enrolment period that opened in November 2026. The answer names which year's poverty guidelines that coverage year uses, which is not the same number.

household_size.description: People in the TAX household -- the taxpayer, a spouse filing jointly, and everyone claimed as a dependent. Not the number of people living in the home and not the number enrolling in a plan.

income.description: Optional: the household's expected modified adjusted gross income for the coverage year, in dollars. With it the answer also states the income as a percentage of the poverty line, which band it falls in and the distance to the top line. Without it the thresholds come back on their own.

state.description: A US state or the District of Columbia, by name, e.g. "Texas", "Alaska" or "District of Columbia". Matched case-insensitively against our own state records; a near miss gets the candidates back rather than the nearest one's figures. It decides which of the three HHS poverty guideline tables applies and brings that state's own marketplace record with it.
